claims.text: The Racial Diversity UK Fund (RDUK) supports research on racial diversity within the UK.
Grants from £15,000 to £500,000 are available.
There is one deadline a year for this fund, in the Autumn.
The next deadline is 5 October 2026.
The priority theme for 2026 applications is Inter-generational changes, continuities and challenges in racially diverse UK.
The fund is interested in generational shifts in outlooks, experiences and conditions and their implications for the UK’s racially diverse future.
The fund is interested in issues of identities, belonging and exclusions, aspirations and values, civic and political participation, and life chances and experiences.
The fund is interested in the future of UK society as shaped by its colonial past, specifically by the migration of people from former British colonies to the UK.
The fund expects research to contribute to understanding, public debate, policy and/or practice on tackling racial inequalities, discrimination and disadvantage.
The fund expects research to map pathways towards a UK that is comfortable with and reaping the benefits of its growing racial diversity.
The fund encourages applicants from diverse backgrounds, particularly from individuals and organisations from racially minoritised communities.
The fund strongly encourages partnership applications which bring together researchers and racially minoritised communities.
Potential applicants can discuss research ideas with the fund, including at early stages.
Contact RDUK@nuffieldfoundation.org to discuss research ideas.

claims.text: Applicants must be employed by or have a formal affiliation with a UK-based organisation.
The UK-based organisation must be a university, research organisation, or voluntary sector body.
The affiliation or employment must last for at least the duration of the project.
Unaffiliated individuals are excluded.
Projects led by schools or FE colleges are excluded.
Undergraduates or master's students are excluded.
PhD-fee projects are excluded.
Establishment of academic posts is excluded.
Non-UK-led organisations are excluded, except in exceptional circumstances for overseas hosts.
Proposals must address at least one of the priority questions.
Proposals must meet the assessment criteria.
Proposals from individuals without formal employment or contractual relationship with the institution hosting the grant are not eligible.
